t: You're looking at a memorial to Baron Paul Julius von Reuter. It was designed by Theo Crosby, a South African-born architect and writer, and a founding partner of the design firm Pentagram. Crosby also drew up the reconstruction of Shakespeare's Globe in London, so he knew a thing or two about rebuilding the past. The carving was done by Michael Black, an English sculptor who lived in Oxford and is best known for the Emperors' Heads outside the Sheldonian Theatre there. A fine piece of collaboration between an architect and a carver.
